svg.title: Cogniva — master architecture and request lifecycle
svg.desc: Connected process diagram showing administrator PDF ingestion, organization-scoped retrieval, factual verification, policy rule evaluation using Laya and TypeScript, and the response rendered with json-render.
svg.text: Master architecture · follow the data from PDF to supported answer
Solid arrows = request flow · dashed arrow = stored evidence

g.text: Admin-only upload · validation · local extraction · atomic indexing
Assistant token → organization → its ready source pages
Draft → separate review → deterministic source checks
Source requirements → visitor facts → typed checks → code-owned verdict

g.title: Upload organization PDFs — An authenticated administrator uploads a PDF through the dashboard. Documents can be replaced, deleted, or retried after failed processing.

Authorize administrator — The server resolves the signed-in organization and requires owner or admin membership. File operations are scoped by that organization, not by a visitor-supplied organization ID.

Validate and reserve upload — The server validates bytes, filename, PDF readability, file size, page count, and the organization quota. It reserves a processing record with the original PDF bytes before extraction.
Extract each page — pdf-lib separates pages and AnyDoc extracts Markdown locally. Text-based PDFs are supported; this application does not add an OCR stage.
Chunk with page context — The server splits page text into overlapping passages. Each chunk retains organization ID, document ID, and its original page number.

Organization knowledge base — One local SQLite database stores all organizations. The publish transaction adds passages, updates the search index through triggers, and marks the document ready. Replacing a ready PDF removes the old version only when the new version publishes successfully.
Ask a question — The assistant reads its token from the URL fragment and sends it in the request body. Chat history is displayed locally; each backend question is evaluated independently.

Identify organization — The API hashes and validates the assistant token to resolve the organization, then rate-limits requests for that organization. Simple greetings, thanks, and identity questions are answered directly without retrieval or a model call.

Retrieve source pages — Keyword search uses English stemming, ranks matching chunks, and reconstructs up to six full pages. Both search and policy expansion use organization filters. No matches return no_answer; excessive source context returns unresolved.

Route the request — The model classifies the question and selects actual evidence IDs. Application guards keep general and procedural requests factual and route clear personalized eligibility requests through policy checks. The planner does not decide eligibility.
Draft cited claims — The composer drafts claims for each question part using retrieved pages. Every claim carries a page evidence ID and candidate source quote. Unsupported parts have no claims.

Review drafted claims — A second call checks each candidate claim for support, relevance to the question, and relevance of its quote. It can select a corrected contiguous excerpt from the same cited page. This is another model judgment, not a proof of correctness.

Validate source quotations — Code confirms the selected quote exists on the actual page and checks quantities with units and currencies. A numeric paraphrase falls back to the source wording only after semantic checks pass. Supported parts remain visible alongside gaps; inconclusive verification returns unresolved.

Expand policy context — The server loads every page of selected policy documents and follows exact document-title cross-references within the same organization. Reading limits stop an oversized policy with unresolved instead of silently truncating it.

Build required-rule ledger — English requirement and prohibition heuristics build a fixed ledger before matching visitor facts. The planner cannot remove conditions. Recognized complex structures and oversized or empty ledgers return unresolved; this is not a general-purpose policy compiler.

Match visitor facts to rules — The schema requires every ledger ID. The model copies exact contiguous visitor excerpts and preserves quantities and units. Missing facts stay missing. A bounded numeric correction can select only numbered excerpts from the real question.

Check rule applicability — Laya Choice classifies whether the source rule category applies. A Boolean applicability check corroborates exclusions. Excluded rules stay in the decision trace; uncertain applicability cannot approve a request. Laya calls are batched and serialized by the adapter.

Evaluate semantic conditions — Boolean checks assess whether the fact addresses the rule, establishes compliance, or establishes an explicit violation. Lack of evidence is not a violation. Conflicting or inconclusive outcomes remain uncertain; scores are thresholds, not calibrated correctness probabilities.

Evaluate numeric conditions — Code evaluates supported numeric thresholds, ranges, allowed values, and compatible units or scales. The visitor value must address the rule subject; unsafe interpretation stays uncertain. There are no hardcoded organization-specific policy cases.

Combine results + explain — Code rejects when any applicable condition fails, asks for missing facts when no failure is established, and approves only when applicable checks exist and all pass. Otherwise it returns unresolved. The composer receives the computed verdict and checks; decision text retains verified policy excerpts, and code keeps the verdict authoritative.

Return response JSON — The API returns one of answered, needs_clarification, unresolved, no_answer, or acknowledged. Calculated decisions can include the verdict and check trace. Transport or provider failures remain errors; they are not disguised as successful answers.

Display evidence and outcome — The client maps verified API data into a small read-only json-render catalog. Zod validates props and a direct fallback preserves the response if validation fails. Citation links reveal page excerpts without replacing the token fragment. The model does not generate UI layout.

g.text: One SQLite database; every document read
and write is scoped by organization ID.
